newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-KONSTANTINOV REMAINS IN CRITICAL CONDITION.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-KONSTANTINOV REMAINS IN CRITICAL CONDITION.

text.p: Detroit Red Wings star defenceman Vladimir Konstantinov remained unconscious in critical condition Monday with head injuries suffered in a Friday night limousine crash, his doctors said.
"The good news is there's been no significant deterioration," Dr. James Robbins said, noting Konstantinov was showing mild responses to music and other stimuli.
"These responses are somewhat inconsistent and they do not mean we expect rapid and steady improvement," Robbins cautioned the Russian star's teammates and reporters at a news conference.

Konstantinov, 30, and fellow Red Wings star Slava Fetisov, 39, two of the team's vaunted "Russian five" unit, were injured Friday night when the stretch limousine they were riding in crashed head-on into a tree. The team's 43-year-old Russian masseur, Sergei Mnatsakanov, also suffered severe head injuries in the one-vehicle accident and was in a coma.
Fetisov was less severely injured and was expected to be released from the hospital soon, doctors said.

Investigators were focusing on the limousine driver, Richard Gnida, who they said may have fallen asleep at the wheel on a main road in suburban Birmingham while returning from a team golf outing. The impact with a tree crumpled the front of the limousine.

"The road was clear. He knew that no one cut him off. The next thing he remembers is striking the curb and trying to steer around objects in the median," Birmingham Deputy Police Chief Richard Patterson said.
"We have preliminary information that he fell asleep," Patterson said.
Investigators were also looking at Gnida's checkered driving record. At the time of the accident, he was driving the limousine despite having had his drivers' licence revoked.
The accident occurred just six days after the team captured its first Stanley Cup championship since 1955.

Konstantinov anchored the Red Wing's brilliant defensive play throughout the run to the Stanley Cup. He also is a finalist for the Norris Trophy, awarded annually to the NHL's best defenceman. The award winner will be announced Thursday night in Toronto.
Grieving fans, who less than a week ago honoured the Red Wings with a victory parade, laid get-well cards and mementos at the crash site and some kept vigil at the hospital.
